nodes.description: Acinar cells can lose differentiated identity and adopt ductal-like programs during injury and KRAS-driven transformation. ADM is reversible in regenerative settings and is not synonymous with cancer. Persistent oncogenic signaling can channel reprogrammed cells into PanIN. Adult ductal cells can also initiate PDAC with cooperating p53 alterations in mice; the relative contribution of these origins in humans remains unresolved.

evidence.reference_title: Ductal metaplasia in pancreas.
evidence.snippet: Acinar to ductal metaplasia (ADM) is the predominant form of ductal metaplasia in pancreas.

evidence.reference_title: Chronic pancreatitis is essential for induction of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma by K-Ras oncogenes in adult mice.
evidence.snippet: suggesting that PDA originates by differentiation of acinar/centroacinar cells or their precursors into ductal-like cells

evidence.reference_title: p53 mutations cooperate with oncogenic Kras to promote adenocarcinoma from pancreatic ductal cells.
evidence.snippet: These data demonstrate that pancreatic ductal cells, whereas exhibiting relative resistance to oncogenic Kras alone, can serve as an effective cell of origin for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma in the setting of gain-of-function mutations in p53.

nodes.description: Daraxonrasib can initially control PDAC and subsequently lose efficacy through heterogeneous resistance routes. An August 2026 study profiled 44 patients with response or stable disease lasting more than three months followed by progression: 59% had treatment-emergent RAS-pathway genomic alterations, including KRAS amplification in 36%. Mutant-allele identity was inferred from variant-allele-frequency ratios by an exploratory method, not directly confirmed in all cases. These selected-cohort findings establish patient mechanisms but not universal resistance or population-wide route frequencies. Median progression-free survival alone cannot distinguish acquired resistance, primary nonresponse and death. Non-genomic, tissue-specific and low-shedding routes remain incompletely captured.

evidence.reference_title: Acquired resistance to the RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibitor daraxonrasib guides rational combination therapy strategies in pancreatic cancer.
evidence.snippet: Here we report mechanisms of acquired resistance to daraxonrasib monotherapy observed through targeted sequencing of over 800 genes in paired pretreatment and end of treatment circulating tumor DNA samples from 44 patients in the phase 1/2 clinical trial.

evidence.reference_title: Acquired resistance to the RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibitor daraxonrasib guides rational combination therapy strategies in pancreatic cancer.
evidence.snippet: Treatment-emergent genomic alterations in the RAS signaling pathway were observed in more than half (26 of 44; 59%) of these patients, including, most notably, mutant KRAS amplifications in one-third (16 of 44; 36%), as well as alterations in receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) (4 of 44; 9%), MAPK (11 of 44; 25%) and PI3K (4 of 44; 9%) pathways.

evidence.reference_title: Acquired resistance to the RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibitor daraxonrasib guides rational combination therapy strategies in pancreatic cancer.
evidence.snippet: Notably, no acquired secondary KRAS mutations were observed, distinct from resistance profiles of mutant-selective KRAS G12C(OFF) inhibitors.

nodes.description: In KRAS-G12C-driven mouse PDAC, selective KRAS inhibition upregulated the CD24 antiphagocytic signal despite an inflamed microenvironment. CD24 blockade increased macrophage phagocytosis and sensitized tumors; related findings occurred in G12D PDAC. The preprint and final paper report the same work. This is a plausible immune-adaptation route whose relevance to clinical daraxonrasib progression remains unproven.

evidence.reference_title: KRAS Inhibition Activates an Actionable CD24 "Do Not Eat Me" Signal in Pancreatic Cancer.
evidence.snippet: Blocking CD24 enhanced macrophage phagocytosis of cancer cells and significantly sensitized tumors to G12Ci treatment.

nodes.description: CRISPR screens identify mTOR and JUN as convergent mediators of resistance to MAPK-pathway inhibitor combinations. In PDAC cells, JUN overexpression supported resistance to SHP2 plus RMC-6236; in-vivo MAP2K4 rescue used SHP2 plus ERK inhibition. The combination-specific evidence should not be recast as patient-level daraxonrasib monotherapy resistance. A separate RMC-7977 mouse study identified focal Jun gain in one resistant tumor.
nodes.id: Adaptive mTOR and JUN-AP1 Transcriptional Program

evidence.reference_title: CRISPR knockout screens reveal JUN as the master mediator of resistance to MAPK inhibition in KRAS-mutant pancreatic cancer.
evidence.snippet: Through unbiased CRISPR-based screenings, we identified mTOR and JUN hyperactivation as interconnected mechanisms that overcome MAPK suppression.

evidence.reference_title: CRISPR knockout screens reveal JUN as the master mediator of resistance to MAPK inhibition in KRAS-mutant pancreatic cancer.
evidence.snippet: Alterations in the PI3K/AKT/mTOR and JUN pathways can induce resistance to multiple combinations of MAPK pathway inhibitors

nodes.description: RMC-7977 increased MHC-I on residual malignant cells in a syngeneic PDAC model. This is direct evidence for a RAS(ON)-associated antigen-presentation change in PDAC, although the relative mediation by autophagy, FAK, interferon signaling and tumor selection remains unresolved. NSCLC daraxonrasib-elironrasib results are supplementary cross-cancer evidence, not the sole anchor.

evidence.reference_title: T-cell Dependency of Tumor Regressions and Complete Responses with RAS(ON) Multi-selective Inhibition in Preclinical Models of Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.
evidence.snippet: the tumor cells that remained exhibited increased expression of MHC class I

nodes.description: Basal autophagy can maintain oxidative metabolism and restrain damaging reactive oxygen species in established pancreatic cancer models. Recycling also provides substrates under treatment stress. The effects of autophagy loss differ by tumor stage and genetic context; preclinical dependency is not a validated universal treatment response.

evidence.reference_title: Pancreatic cancers require autophagy for tumor growth.
evidence.snippet: Genetic or pharmacologic inhibition of autophagy leads to increased reactive oxygen species, elevated DNA damage, and a metabolic defect leading to decreased mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation.

nodes.description: Basal malignant cells can organize tumor-maintaining fibroblast, macrophage and cytokine states. Lineage tracing found greater plasticity of basal than classical cells in autochthonous mouse PDAC. Basal-state ablation, and separately basal-cell GM-CSF knockout, reprogrammed the stroma and recruited cytotoxic lymphocytes. This establishes a causal circuit in these models while leaving human state-targeting efficacy unresolved.

evidence.reference_title: The basal cell state maintains pancreatic cancers by controlling an immunosuppressive circuit.
evidence.snippet: Knockout of a single cytokine, GM-CSF, specifically in basal cells recapitulated macrophage repolarization and lymphocyte recruitment observed upon basal state ablation and shrank tumors.

nodes.description: Endoscopic placement of a fully covered self-expandable metallic biliary stent can relieve malignant biliary obstruction. Select procedural drainage according to anatomy, symptoms and the clinical treatment plan.

evidence.reference_title: Pan-Asian adapted ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines for the diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of patients with pancreatic cancer.
evidence.snippet: In the event of biliary obstruction, endoscopic placement of a fully covered, self-expandable metallic biliary stent is suggested

nodes.description: FAP-positive fibroblasts can supply CXCL12 that localizes around malignant cells and limits T-cell access. In KPC mouse tumors, CXCR4 inhibition rapidly increased T-cell accumulation and synergized with PD-L1 blockade. This identifies a specific stromal immune-exclusion circuit, not uniform behavior of all fibroblasts.

biological_processes: Negative Regulation of T Cell Mediated Immunity

evidence.reference_title: Targeting CXCL12 from FAP-expressing carcinoma-associated fibroblasts synergizes with anti-PD-L1 immunotherapy in pancreatic cancer.
evidence.snippet: Administering AMD3100, a CXCL12 receptor chemokine (C-X-C motif) receptor 4 inhibitor, induced rapid T-cell accumulation among cancer cells and acted synergistically with α-PD-L1 to greatly diminish cancer cells

nodes.description: Long-term MRTX1133 treatment can reverse early immune infiltration through CDK8-associated CXCL2 secretion and FAS suppression. CDK8 perturbation restores immune control in those PDAC models. Daraxonrasib-resistant PDX tumors also show CDK8 upregulation, but this does not establish the entire temporal CXCL2/FAS immune circuit under daraxonrasib or in patients.

evidence.reference_title: CDK8 remodels the tumor microenvironment and promotes resistance to KRAS(G12D) inhibitors and daraxonrasib in PDAC.
evidence.snippet: CDK8 imparts this resistance via induction of CXCL2 chemokine secretion, inhibition of FAS expression, and remodeling of the TME to promote immune evasion.

evidence.reference_title: CDK8 remodels the tumor microenvironment and promotes resistance to KRAS(G12D) inhibitors and daraxonrasib in PDAC.
evidence.snippet: We also provide evidence of CDK8 upregulation in PDX tumors resistant to inhibitors selective for RAS(ON) and RASG12D(ON): daraxonrasib and zoldonrasib, respectively

nodes.description: Inflammation and tissue injury can cooperate with oncogenic KRAS to enable acinar reprogramming and precursor formation. In one adult acinar/centroacinar KRAS-G12V mouse model, chronic pancreatitis was necessary for tumor induction. This is a model-specific requirement, not a claim that every human PDAC requires clinically recognized pancreatitis. Human chronic pancreatitis is a strong risk factor with risk estimates dependent on follow-up and case definition.

evidence.reference_title: Chronic pancreatitis is essential for induction of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma by K-Ras oncogenes in adult mice.
evidence.snippet: These observations suggest that, during adulthood, PDA stems from a combination of genetic (e.g., somatic K-Ras mutations) and nongenetic (e.g., tissue damage) events.

evidence.reference_title: Chronic Pancreatitis Is a Risk Factor for Pancreatic Cancer, and Incidence Increases With Duration of Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
evidence.snippet: There is an increased risk of PDAC in patients with CP, and incidence rates increase with CP disease duration.

nodes.description: A preprint reports reduced cyclophilin-A protein with retained KRAS-G12D-GTP signaling in daraxonrasib-resistant PDAC cells. As cyclophilin A is required for tri-complex formation, reduced availability is a plausible drug-engagement escape mechanism. This observation does not establish that peptidyl-prolyl isomerase catalytic activity was measured or is causally required. The single clinical case in this paper instead concerns KRAS-G12R EGFR/wild-type-RAS activation.
nodes.id: Cyclophilin A Loss and Reduced Tri-Complex Engagement

evidence.reference_title: Overcoming Daraxonrasib Resistance: Allele-Specific Mechanisms Guide Salvage Therapy in Pancreatic Cancer.
evidence.snippet: In contrast, KRAS G12D resistance arose through retained KRAS G12D -GTP signaling, with a decrease of cyclophilin A (CypA) protein, the binding partner required for daraxonrasib activity.

nodes.description: Daraxonrasib is a cyclophilin-A-dependent inhibitor of active GTP-bound mutant and wild-type RAS. In phase III RASolute 302 for previously treated metastatic PDAC, median overall survival was 13.2 versus 6.6 months in the RAS G12 population (hazard ratio 0.40); median progression-free survival was 7.3 versus 3.5 months. These clinical outcomes establish treatment efficacy, not a universal resistance mechanism or an immune basis for survival benefit.

evidence.reference_title: RASolute 302: A Phase 3 Multicenter, Open-label, Randomized Study of Daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) Versus Investigator's Choice of Standard of Care Therapy in Patients With Previously Treated Metastatic Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma (PDAC)
evidence.snippet: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the safety and efficacy of a novel RAS(ON) inhibitor compared to standard(s) of care (SOC) treatment.

evidence.reference_title: Daraxonrasib or Chemotherapy in Previously Treated Metastatic Pancreatic Cancer.
evidence.snippet: Daraxonrasib is an oral RAS(ON) multiselective, tri-complex inhibitor of the active guanosine triphosphate-bound state of mutant and wild-type RAS.

evidence.reference_title: Daraxonrasib or Chemotherapy in Previously Treated Metastatic Pancreatic Cancer.
evidence.snippet: The median overall survival in the RAS G12 population was 13.2 months with daraxonrasib and 6.6 months with chemotherapy, and the median overall survival in the overall population was 13.2 months and 6.7 months, respectively; the hazard ratio was 0.40 in both populations (P<0.001).

nodes.description: Tumor-derived signals and local tissue interactions recruit and alter fibroblast states that deposit collagen, hyaluronan and other extracellular matrix. Dense matrix can impair perfusion, but stromal programs are heterogeneous: some support inflammation or immune exclusion and others restrain tumor growth. Fibroblast depletion and matrix digestion are not interchangeable, and neither is a generally validated treatment for PDAC.

evidence.snippet: Here, we use organoid and mouse models to identify TGFβ and IL1 as tumor-secreted ligands that promote CAF heterogeneity.

nodes.description: Epithelial-mesenchymal plasticity can accompany dissemination and drug resistance, but individual EMT transcription factors have nonredundant roles. Snail or Twist deletion did not abolish metastasis in a KPC study. Early dissemination observed in mouse precursor models is not proof that all human PDAC metastasizes before invasion.

evidence.reference_title: EMT and dissemination precede pancreatic tumor formation.
evidence.snippet: Tagged cells invaded and entered the bloodstream unexpectedly early, before frank malignancy could be detected by rigorous histologic analysis; this behavior was widely associated with epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT).

evidence.reference_title: Epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition is dispensable for metastasis but induces chemoresistance in pancreatic cancer.
evidence.snippet: EMT suppression in the primary tumour does not alter the emergence of invasive PDAC, systemic dissemination or metastasis.

nodes.description: Reduced pancreatic digestive enzyme delivery contributes to maldigestion, malnutrition and weight loss, particularly with advanced or pancreatic-head disease.

evidence.reference_title: Pancreatic exocrine insufficiency and pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy in patients with advanced pancreatic cancer: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
evidence.snippet: The pooled prevalence of pancreatic exocrine insufficiency in advanced pancreatic cancer was 72% (95% confidence interval: 55-86%)

nodes.description: PDAC-derived exosomes carrying MIF can be taken up by Kupffer cells, inducing TGF-beta, hepatic stellate-cell fibronectin deposition and recruitment of bone-marrow-derived macrophages. This establishes a liver premetastatic niche mechanism; the cited study does not by itself establish direct exosomal suppression of dendritic cells or T cells.

evidence.reference_title: Pancreatic cancer exosomes initiate pre-metastatic niche formation in the liver.
evidence.snippet: Uptake of PDAC-derived exosomes by Kupffer cells caused transforming growth factor β secretion and upregulation of fibronectin production by hepatic stellate cells. This fibrotic microenvironment enhanced recruitment of bone marrow-derived macrophages.

evidence.reference_title: Pancreatic cancer exosomes initiate pre-metastatic niche formation in the liver.
evidence.snippet: We found that macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) was highly expressed in PDAC-derived exosomes, and its blockade prevented liver pre-metastatic niche formation and metastasis.

nodes.description: Checkpoint combinations with RAS inhibitors are supported by mouse PDAC experiments. RMC-7977/daraxonrasib plus PD-1-based therapy worked in one study, whereas a later study found CTLA-4 blockade specifically effective and associated with Treg reprogramming and tertiary lymphoid structures. Regimen, model, timing and checkpoint partner matter. These results do not establish routine clinical daraxonrasib-checkpoint treatment.
nodes.id: Experimental KRAS Inhibition with Immune Checkpoint Blockade

evidence.reference_title: Oncogenic Kras targeting with MRTX1133 or Daraxonrasib specifically synergize with anti-CTLA4 to promote anti-tumor immunity in pancreatic cancer
evidence.snippet: Kras* inhibition induces T-cell influx and offers a therapeutic window to specifically prime PDAC to anti-CTLA4 immune checkpoint blockade efficacy, in contrast to anti-PD1, anti-Tim3, anti-Lag3, anti-Vista, and anti-4-1BB agonist combination therapy.

nodes.description: Daraxonrasib, afatinib and the STAT3 degrader SD36 produced prolonged regressions in orthotopic, genetically engineered and patient-derived xenograft PDAC models. This corrected primary study also tested genetic RAF1/EGFR/STAT3 ablation. It supports combination research, not routine patient treatment or proof that immunity is irrelevant.

evidence.reference_title: A targeted combination therapy achieves effective pancreatic cancer regression and prevents tumor resistance.
evidence.snippet: a combination of selective inhibitors of KRAS (RMC-6236/daraxonrasib), EGFR family (afatinib), and STAT3 (SD36) induced the complete regression of orthotopic PDAC tumors with no evidence of tumor resistance for over 200 d posttreatment.

nodes.description: Tumor-cell FAK signaling limits immunoproteasome expression and antigen presentation in PDAC models. FAK depletion increases antigen diversity and MHC-I presentation; combined STAT3 loss further promotes immune control. This is a complementary regulator, not evidence that RAS cannot influence MHC-I. The reported antigen-presentation effect is kinase-independent, requires nuclear FAK, and is lost in an extreme squamous phenotype; FAK kinase inhibition is therefore not equivalent to eliminating this function.

evidence.reference_title: FAK suppresses antigen processing and presentation to promote immune evasion in pancreatic cancer.
evidence.snippet: Loss of PDAC cell-intrinsic FAK signalling promotes expression of the immunoproteasome and Major Histocompatibility Complex class-I (MHC-I), resulting in increased antigen diversity and antigen presentation by FAK-/- PDAC cells.

nodes.description: Liver is a common metastatic site. The cited registry estimate of 74.36% concerns synchronous metastatic cases, not all PDAC or all patients with locally advanced disease.

evidence.reference_title: A population-based study of synchronous distant metastases and prognosis in patients with PDAC at initial diagnosis.
evidence.snippet: There was a highest incidence of liver metastases from pancreatic cancer (2387,74.36%), followed by lung (625,19.47%), bone (190,5.92%), and brain (8,0.25%).

nodes.description: Patient-derived PDAC organoids and established cell models permit driver-specific RMC-7977 sensitivity assays; engineered and selected cell models test bypass mechanisms. These isolated epithelial systems do not reproduce the complete immune or desmoplastic microenvironment.
nodes.id: Human PDAC Cell and Organoid RAS-Response Models

evidence.reference_title: Tumour-selective activity of RAS-GTP inhibition in pancreatic cancer.
evidence.snippet: RMC-7977 exhibited low nanomolar potency on the viability of most human and mouse PDAC cell lines and human PDAC organoids

nodes.description: Tumor-derived IL1 induces fibroblast LIF and JAK-STAT signaling, promoting an inflammatory CAF state. TGF-beta antagonizes this program by reducing IL1R1 and favoring myofibroblasts. Spatial exposure and plasticity generate distinct CAF niches, so fibroblast number alone is an inadequate mechanistic readout.

evidence.reference_title: IL1-Induced JAK/STAT Signaling Is Antagonized by TGFβ to Shape CAF Heterogeneity in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.
evidence.snippet: We show that IL1 induces LIF expression and downstream JAK/STAT activation to generate inflammatory CAFs and demonstrate that TGFβ antagonizes this process by downregulating IL1R1 expression and promoting differentiation into myofibroblasts.

nodes.description: SOS1 plus MEK blockade increased CD8 infiltration but also generated IL6-positive inflammatory CAFs, M2-like macrophages and poorer dendritic-cell function in KPCY models. CD40 agonism reactivated myeloid cells and enabled durable checkpoint combinations. This qualifies a uniformly beneficial RAS-inhibition model but is not direct daraxonrasib evidence.
nodes.id: IL6-CAF and Myeloid Rebound after SOS1-MEK Inhibition

evidence.reference_title: Reshaping the Tumor Microenvironment of KRASG12D Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma with Combined SOS1 and MEK Inhibition for Improved Immunotherapy Response.
evidence.snippet: revealed an increase in inflammatory cancer-associated fibroblasts (iCAF), M2 macrophages, and a decreased dendritic cell (DC) quality

nodes.description: Myeloid suppression, dysfunctional lymphocytes, stromal exclusion and impaired antigen presentation limit immune control in most PDAC. These mechanisms vary between tumors and metastatic sites. Rare mismatch-repair-deficient/MSI-high cancers can respond to checkpoint blockade; PDAC is not uniformly refractory to every immune or targeted therapy.

evidence.reference_title: Molecular and metabolic regulation of immunosuppression in metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
evidence.snippet: Immunosuppression is a hallmark of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), contributing to early metastasis and poor patient survival.

evidence.reference_title: Molecular and metabolic regulation of immunosuppression in metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
evidence.snippet: Following chemokine and exosomal guidance, these cells metastasize to the organ-specific pre-metastatic niches (PMNs) constituted by local resident cells, stromal fibroblasts, and suppressive immune cells, such as the metastasis-associated macrophages, neutrophils, and myeloid-derived suppressor cells.

nodes.description: RMC-7977 and daraxonrasib experiments test tumor regression, immune-cell changes and immunotherapy combinations in immunocompetent PDAC. Results depend on regimen and tumor/host model and do not establish patient immune pharmacodynamics.

evidence.reference_title: T-cell Dependency of Tumor Regressions and Complete Responses with RAS(ON) Multi-selective Inhibition in Preclinical Models of Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.
evidence.snippet: In this study, we report that RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibition led to rapid and profound PDAC regressions in immunocompetent mice, decreasing myeloid cells and increasing T cells and macrophages in the tumor microenvironment.

nodes.description: In immunocompetent PDAC models, RAS(ON) multiselective inhibition can reduce suppressive myeloid subsets, increase tumor MHC-I and lymphocyte infiltration, and enable immune-dependent tumor control. RMC-7977 and daraxonrasib provide direct PDAC evidence. Responses and optimal checkpoint partners are model-dependent; increased Tregs and adaptive myeloid rebound can limit benefit. Patient survival from daraxonrasib monotherapy does not establish an immune-mediated clinical benefit.
nodes.id: Immunosuppressive TME Reversibility under RAS(ON) Inhibition

evidence.snippet: In this study, we report that RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibition led to rapid and profound PDAC regressions in immunocompetent mice, decreasing myeloid cells and increasing T cells and macrophages in the tumor microenvironment.

evidence.reference_title: T-cell Dependency of Tumor Regressions and Complete Responses with RAS(ON) Multi-selective Inhibition in Preclinical Models of Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.
evidence.snippet: The depth and duration of tumor regression depended on T cells and conventional dendritic cells.

nodes.description: Chronic RMC-7977 exposure produces initially responding and subsequently relapsing KPC tumors. MYC and YAP/TEAD programs were interrogated; tool-compound models and clinical daraxonrasib cohorts have different resistance distributions.

evidence.reference_title: Tumour-selective activity of RAS-GTP inhibition in pancreatic cancer.
evidence.snippet: Analysis of relapsed tumours identified Myc copy number gain as a prevalent candidate resistance mechanism, which could be overcome by combinatorial TEAD inhibition in vitro.

nodes.description: Activating KRAS variants favor persistent RAS-GTP signaling through RAF-MEK-ERK and additional effector networks, supporting proliferation, survival, metabolic rewiring and microenvironmental remodeling. G12D, G12V and G12R are common in PDAC, with allele-specific signaling and inhibitor responses. Most PDACs are KRAS-mutant; KRAS-wild-type cancers require separate driver characterization. KRAS signaling does not itself establish acquisition of a particular tumor-suppressor mutation or therapeutic inhibition.

evidence.reference_title: Molecular Characterization of KRAS Wild-type Tumors in Patients with Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma.
evidence.snippet: KRAS mutation (MT) is a major oncogenic driver in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC).

evidence.reference_title: Targeting KRAS mutations in pancreatic cancer: opportunities for future strategies
evidence.snippet: In the case of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinomas (PDAC), 90–92% harbor mutations in the oncogene KRAS, triggering canonical MAPK signaling.

evidence.reference_title: From precursor to cancer: decoding the intrinsic and extrinsic pathways of pancreatic intraepithelial neoplasia progression
evidence.snippet: PanIN development begins with Kirsten rat sarcoma viral oncogene (KRAS) mutations driving PanIN initiation. Key additional mutations in cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor 2A (CDKN2A), tumor protein p53 (TP53), and mothers against decapentaplegic homolog 4 (SMAD4) disrupt cell cycle control and genomic stability, crucial for PanIN progression from low-grade to high-grade dysplasia.

nodes.description: KRAS supports glucose uptake and redirects intermediates toward anabolic pathways that sustain pancreatic tumor growth. This is a regulated metabolic program rather than a universal switch eliminating oxidative phosphorylation.

evidence.reference_title: Oncogenic Kras maintains pancreatic tumors through regulation of anabolic glucose metabolism.
evidence.snippet: Transcriptome and metabolomic analyses indicate that Kras(G12D) serves a vital role in controlling tumor metabolism through stimulation of glucose uptake and channeling of glucose intermediates into the hexosamine biosynthesis and pentose phosphate pathways (PPP).

nodes.description: Oncogenic KRAS induces tumor-cell GM-CSF, expanding suppressive myeloid cells that constrain cytotoxic T-cell immunity in pancreatic neoplasia models. This supplies a disease-driving counterpart to the myeloid remodeling seen after KRAS inhibition.

evidence.reference_title: Oncogenic Kras-induced GM-CSF production promotes the development of pancreatic neoplasia.
evidence.snippet: Kras(G12D)-dependent production of GM-CSF in vivo is required for the recruitment of Gr1(+)CD11b(+) myeloid cells.

nodes.description: In studied PDAC cells, glutamine-derived aspartate is routed through cytosolic GOT1, malate and pyruvate to support NADPH-dependent redox balance. Dependency varies with growth context and compensatory metabolism; this does not establish clinical efficacy of glutaminase inhibition.

evidence.reference_title: Glutamine supports pancreatic cancer growth through a KRAS-regulated metabolic pathway.
evidence.snippet: Furthermore, we establish that the reprogramming of glutamine metabolism is mediated by oncogenic KRAS

nodes.description: RMC-7977-resistant KPC tumors frequently gained Myc copies while maintaining ERK suppression. YAP-TEAD-dependent transcriptional output accompanied resistance, and TEAD cotargeting restored sensitivity in vitro. The subsequent daraxonrasib clinical study detected MYC amplification in one patient together with KRAS amplification and corroborated MYC-related resistance in models. These data support a bypass route without proving that all MYC gain is independent of RAS or that TEAD combinations benefit patients.

animal_models.description: Tracks relapse-associated MYC amplification and downstream bypass.
animal_models.name: KPC RMC-7977 Acquired-Resistance Models

evidence.reference_title: Tumour-selective activity of RAS-GTP inhibition in pancreatic cancer.
evidence.snippet: Analysis of relapsed tumours identified Myc copy number gain as a prevalent candidate resistance mechanism, which could be overcome by combinatorial TEAD inhibition in vitro.

evidence.reference_title: Acquired resistance to the RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibitor daraxonrasib guides rational combination therapy strategies in pancreatic cancer.
evidence.snippet: We also observed truncating mutations in NF1 (2 of 44; 4%), KEAP1 (2 of 44; 4%), a PTPN11 mutation or MYC amplification in one patient each (1 of 44; 2%).

nodes.description: RAS-driven macropinocytosis internalizes extracellular protein for lysosomal proteolysis and amino-acid supply. It supports growth in nutrient-poor settings and is observed in primary human PDAC specimens, complementing transport of free nutrients.

evidence.reference_title: Macropinocytosis of protein is an amino acid supply route in Ras-transformed cells.
evidence.snippet: The internalized protein undergoes proteolytic degradation, yielding amino acids including glutamine that can enter central carbon metabolism.

evidence.reference_title: Human pancreatic cancer tumors are nutrient poor and tumor cells actively scavenge extracellular protein.
evidence.snippet: Consistent with this hypothesis, active macropinocytosis is observed in primary human PDAC specimens.

nodes.description: Hyaluronan-rich stroma can elevate interstitial fluid pressure, collapse vessels and restrict delivery of nutrients and drugs in PDAC mouse models. Matrix degradation improved perfusion experimentally, but the phase III PEGPH20 trial did not improve survival, limiting direct therapeutic extrapolation.

evidence.reference_title: Enzymatic targeting of the stroma ablates physical barriers to treatment of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
evidence.snippet: We show here that this desmoplastic reaction generates inordinately high interstitial fluid pressures (IFPs), exceeding those previously measured or theorized for solid tumors, and induces vascular collapse, while presenting substantial barriers to perfusion, diffusion, and convection of small molecule therapeutics.

nodes.description: Invasive tumor cells disseminate and establish distant lesions, frequently in the liver and also lung or peritoneum. Colonization depends on both tumor-cell programs and organ-specific niches; metastatic-site immune composition differs from the primary tumor. A single EMT program is not obligatory for every metastatic event.

evidence.reference_title: Pancreatic cancer exosomes initiate pre-metastatic niche formation in the liver.
evidence.snippet: Here, we show that PDAC-derived exosomes induce liver pre-metastatic niche formation in naive mice and consequently increase liver metastatic burden.

nodes.description: MRTX1133 and RAS(ON) multiselective inhibitors can reduce suppressive myeloid subsets and increase effector lymphocytes in immunocompetent PDAC models. Total macrophage abundance can increase while state composition changes; myeloid remodeling is not equivalent to depletion of every myeloid cell. The direction and durability of individual populations vary by agent, model and time.
nodes.id: Myeloid Suppression Relief and CD8 Effector Infiltration

evidence.reference_title: T-cell Dependency of Tumor Regressions and Complete Responses with RAS(ON) Multi-selective Inhibition in Preclinical Models of Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.
evidence.snippet: In this study, we report that RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibition led to rapid and profound PDAC regressions in immunocompetent mice, decreasing myeloid cells and increasing T cells and macrophages in the tumor microenvironment.

evidence.reference_title: KRAS(G12D) inhibition reprograms the microenvironment of early and advanced pancreatic cancer to promote FAS-mediated killing by CD8(+) T cells.
evidence.snippet: MRTX1133 reverses early PDAC growth, increases intratumoral CD8+ effector T cells, decreases myeloid infiltration, and reprograms cancer-associated fibroblasts.

nodes.description: Selective autophagy directs MHC-I to lysosomes through NBR1, reducing surface antigen presentation and immune recognition in PDAC models. Autophagy inhibition can restore MHC-I and improve T-cell control. This can coexist with RAS-dependent and FAK-dependent regulation; pathway dominance or mutual independence has not been established.

evidence.reference_title: Autophagy promotes immune evasion of pancreatic cancer by degrading MHC-I.
evidence.snippet: Here we show that, in PDAC, MHC-I molecules are selectively targeted for lysosomal degradation by an autophagy-dependent mechanism that involves the autophagy cargo receptor NBR1.

nodes.description: Painless obstructive jaundice is a classic presentation for tumors in the pancreatic head, caused by compression of the common bile duct.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnostic evaluation and staging of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
evidence.snippet: Common signs and symptoms of PDA include abdominal or back pain, jaundice, weight loss, pruritus, and nausea/vomiting.

nodes.description: Increased mutant KRAS dosage can attenuate daraxonrasib suppression and restore RAS-pathway output in PDAC models. Paired ctDNA detected emergent KRAS amplification in 16/44 profiled PDAC patients after initial disease control. Assignment to the pre-existing mutant allele was inferred from variant-allele-frequency ratios; the supplementary table explicitly calls this exploratory and unconfirmed, rather than direct allele phasing in all cases. Engineered and selected PDAC models provide functional corroboration of mutant KRAS dosage. Secondary KRAS mutations were absent from the 44 PDAC cases and selected PDAC resistance models, while an engineered Ba/F3 deep mutational scan identified resistance-conferring second-site variants in a different context.
nodes.id: On-Target RAS Reactivation and KRAS Amplification

evidence.reference_title: Acquired resistance to the RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibitor daraxonrasib guides rational combination therapy strategies in pancreatic cancer.
evidence.snippet: Treatment-emergent genomic alterations in the RAS signaling pathway were observed in more than half (26 of 44; 59%) of these patients, including, most notably, mutant KRAS amplifications in one-third (16 of 44; 36%), as well as alterations in receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) (4 of 44; 9%), MAPK (11 of 44; 25%) and PI3K (4 of 44; 9%) pathways.

evidence.reference_title: Acquired resistance to the RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibitor daraxonrasib guides rational combination therapy strategies in pancreatic cancer.
evidence.snippet: Method is exploratory, and allele amplification is not confirmed.

evidence.reference_title: Acquired resistance to the RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibitor daraxonrasib guides rational combination therapy strategies in pancreatic cancer.
evidence.snippet: To corroborate these clinical findings, we found, or mechanistically established, concordant mechanisms of daraxonrasib resistance in human and murine preclinical models of PDAC, including mutant KRAS and MYC amplification and RTK upregulation, with these alterations guiding various combination therapy concepts.

nodes.description: Grammar-based PhysiCell agent-based model of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma neoplastic cells and cancer-associated fibroblasts. The model encodes fibroblast-mediated invasion, epithelial-mesenchymal state switching, and ECM-dependent motility tradeoffs using human-interpretable cell rules informed by PDAC spatial transcriptomics and coculture data.

Grammar-based PhysiCell agent-based PDAC tumor-immune model initialized from PDAC tissue compositions. The model simulates combination therapy with GVAX, nivolumab, and urelumab across heterogeneous baseline microenvironment states using explicit cell-state and interaction rules.

Pancreatic enzyme replacement, including pancrelipase, is used for exocrine insufficiency and maldigestion when indicated. Mixed observational/trial pooled survival associations do not establish a causal survival benefit; an 88-patient randomized trial of pancrelipase in unresectable pancreatic cancer did not improve the primary eight-week BMI endpoint.

evidence.reference_title: Pancreatic exocrine insufficiency and pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy in patients with advanced pancreatic cancer: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
evidence.snippet: The pooled prevalence of pancreatic exocrine insufficiency in advanced pancreatic cancer was 72% (95% confidence interval: 55-86%)

evidence.reference_title: A Multicenter Open-Label Randomized Controlled Trial of Pancreatic Enzyme Replacement Therapy in Unresectable Pancreatic Cancer.
evidence.snippet: Patients with unresectable PC receiving chemotherapy were randomly assigned to pancrelipase and nonpancrelipase groups.

evidence.reference_title: A Multicenter Open-Label Randomized Controlled Trial of Pancreatic Enzyme Replacement Therapy in Unresectable Pancreatic Cancer.
evidence.snippet: In this randomized controlled trial, pancrelipase failed to improve the change in BMI at 8 weeks in PC patients receiving chemotherapy.

nodes.description: Tumor-associated obstruction and loss of functional pancreatic tissue can impair digestive enzyme delivery. The resulting maldigestion contributes to nutritional loss; this process also occurs after pancreatic surgery. Clinical prevalence varies with stage, location and testing method.

evidence.reference_title: Pancreatic exocrine insufficiency and pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy in patients with advanced pancreatic cancer: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
evidence.snippet: The pooled prevalence of pancreatic exocrine insufficiency in advanced pancreatic cancer was 72% (95% confidence interval: 55-86%)

nodes.description: KRAS-mutant PanIN can progress with cooperating genetic and microenvironmental changes to invasive, gland-forming PDAC. IPMN and mucinous cystic neoplasms provide additional precursor routes. Not every precursor progresses, and a uniform obligatory mutation order or exclusive acinar origin is not established.
nodes.id: Pancreatic Precursor Progression and Invasive Growth

evidence.reference_title: Chronic pancreatitis is essential for induction of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma by K-Ras oncogenes in adult mice.
evidence.snippet: However, if these mice are challenged with a mild form of chronic pancreatitis, they develop the full spectrum of PanINs and invasive PDA.

evidence.reference_title: p53 mutations cooperate with oncogenic Kras to promote adenocarcinoma from pancreatic ductal cells.
evidence.snippet: In contrast to the lack of response to oncogenic Kras alone, simultaneous activation of Kras and mutant p53 in adult ductal epithelium generated invasive PDAC in 75% of mice as early as 2.5 months after tamoxifen administration.

nodes.description: A preprint describes acquired RMC-6236 resistance in mixed PDAC and NSCLC models with sustained cell-cycle progression despite RAS suppression. CDK4/6 or CDK2 cotargeting restored control through distinct arrest programs; CDK2 inhibition produced more durable cytostasis in the tested settings. This is not a clinically validated combination or proof that simultaneous inhibition of all three kinases is required. CDK8-mediated microenvironmental resistance is a separate mechanism.

evidence.reference_title: Targeting Distinct Cell Cycle Nodes Overcomes KRAS/RAS Inhibitor Resistance.
evidence.snippet: While these pathways can be broadly inhibited using the pan-RAS-ON inhibitor RMC-6236, cells remained capable of developing acquired resistance where cell proliferation is uncoupled from RAS signaling.

evidence.reference_title: Targeting Distinct Cell Cycle Nodes Overcomes KRAS/RAS Inhibitor Resistance.
evidence.snippet: Finally, concurrent inhibition of KRAS with either CDK4/6 or CDK2 yields durable tumor control in vivo in xenografts derived from acquired resistant models.

nodes.description: RTK signaling can contribute to daraxonrasib resistance in particular PDAC contexts. The paired 44-patient study found emergent RTK alterations in 4/44, with HER2-upregulated resistant models providing functional support. A separate preprint identified EGFR/wild-type-RAS activation in KRAS-G12R models and one patient who progressed after ten months. G12D cyclophilin-A loss is a distinct route. Earlier MEK or G12C-selective-inhibitor studies are contextual analogies and do not establish universal sufficiency against multiselective inhibition.

evidence.reference_title: Acquired resistance to the RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibitor daraxonrasib guides rational combination therapy strategies in pancreatic cancer.
evidence.snippet: Treatment-emergent genomic alterations in the RAS signaling pathway were observed in more than half (26 of 44; 59%) of these patients, including, most notably, mutant KRAS amplifications in one-third (16 of 44; 36%), as well as alterations in receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) (4 of 44; 9%), MAPK (11 of 44; 25%) and PI3K (4 of 44; 9%) pathways.

evidence.reference_title: Overcoming Daraxonrasib Resistance: Allele-Specific Mechanisms Guide Salvage Therapy in Pancreatic Cancer.
evidence.snippet: KRAS G12R is marked by its inability to transactivate RAS WT , and it was observed that daraxonrasib resistant KRAS G12R PDAC cells utilize EGFR/RAS WT -GTP signaling as the dominant adaptive route.

evidence.reference_title: Overcoming Daraxonrasib Resistance: Allele-Specific Mechanisms Guide Salvage Therapy in Pancreatic Cancer.
evidence.snippet: a KRAS G12R PDAC patient who progressed after 10 months on daraxonrasib showed intratumoral EGFR/RAS WT activation

nodes.description: An August 2026 PDAC study found that MRTX1133 or daraxonrasib recruits regulatory as well as effector and exhausted T cells. In its models, CTLA-4 blockade reprogrammed effector Tregs, reduced CD8 exhaustion and supported tertiary lymphoid structures. Other checkpoint combinations were less effective. This contrasts with a different RMC-7977 model where the CD4 increase was not attributable to FoxP3-positive Tregs, so generalized Treg relief is not supported.
nodes.id: Regulatory T-Cell Recruitment after KRAS Inhibition

evidence.reference_title: Oncogenic Kras targeting with MRTX1133 or Daraxonrasib specifically synergize with anti-CTLA4 to promote anti-tumor immunity in pancreatic cancer
evidence.snippet: Here, we demonstrate that Kras* targeting using MRTX1133 or Daraxonrasib recruits diverse T-cell infiltrates, including regulatory (Tregs), effector and exhausted T cells into the PDAC microenvironment.

evidence.reference_title: T-cell Dependency of Tumor Regressions and Complete Responses with RAS(ON) Multi-selective Inhibition in Preclinical Models of Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.
evidence.snippet: the increase in CD4+ T cells upon RMC-7977 treatment was not attributable to this population

nodes.description: Senescent myofibroblastic CAFs accumulate near tumor ducts and during PDAC progression. Genetic or pharmacologic depletion of senescent stromal cells in mouse models reduced macrophage-associated immune suppression and improved chemotherapy responsiveness. Human tissue identifies the state, but clinical senolytic efficacy is not established.

evidence.reference_title: Senescence Defines a Distinct Subset of Myofibroblasts That Orchestrates Immunosuppression in Pancreatic Cancer
evidence.snippet: Depletion of senescent stromal cells in genetic and pharmacologic PDAC models relieved immune suppression by macrophages, delayed tumor progression, and increased responsiveness to chemotherapy.

nodes.description: Alterations of CDKN2A, TP53 and SMAD4 cooperate with oncogenic signaling. Loss of p16 removes restraint on CDK4/6-RB cell-cycle progression; p53 alterations weaken stress checkpoints and can confer context-dependent gain of function; SMAD4 loss changes TGF-beta responses. Reported alteration frequencies differ with cohort, assay, copy-number detection and inclusion of epigenetic silencing. These are cooperating events rather than consequences inferred from co-occurrence with KRAS.

evidence.reference_title: Core signaling pathways in human pancreatic cancers revealed by global genomic analyses.
evidence.snippet: This list includes the classic tumor suppressor genes CDKN2A (p16), SMAD4, and TP53, as well as genes that had not previously been implicated in pancreatic cancer development.

nodes.description: KRAS-G12D inhibition by MRTX1133 induces FAS in malignant cells and patient-derived organoids, permitting CD8-mediated killing in PDAC models. This is drug- and model-specific evidence; the original citation to the preprint has been replaced with the final paper. CDK8-dependent FAS suppression can later oppose this response.
nodes.id: Tumor-Cell FAS Induction and CD8-Mediated Killing

evidence.reference_title: KRAS(G12D) inhibition reprograms the microenvironment of early and advanced pancreatic cancer to promote FAS-mediated killing by CD8(+) T cells.
evidence.snippet: Mechanistically, inhibition of KRASG12D in advanced PDAC and human patient derived organoids induces FAS expression in cancer cells and facilitates CD8+ T cell-mediated death.

nodes.description: Some fibroblast and stromal programs constrain PDAC. Genetic SHH loss and depletion of alpha-SMA-positive myofibroblasts in distinct mouse models accelerated aggressive disease; newer interferon-response CAF work also identifies a restraining state. These findings qualify global stroma-removal strategies without proving that every myofibroblast state is protective.

evidence.reference_title: Stromal elements act to restrain, rather than support, pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
evidence.snippet: Together, these data demonstrate that some components of the tumor stroma can act to restrain tumor growth.

evidence.reference_title: Depletion of carcinoma-associated fibroblasts and fibrosis induces immunosuppression and accelerates pancreas cancer with reduced survival.
evidence.snippet: Suppressed immune surveillance with increased CD4(+)Foxp3(+) Tregs was observed in myofibroblast-depleted mouse tumors.

nodes.description: KRAS-G12D induces EGR1-USP20, stabilizing HMG-CoA reductase and promoting cholesterol metabolism associated with CD8 exhaustion. KRAS inhibition or cholesterol blockade induces compensatory ULK1-associated autophagy; USP20 also stabilizes ULK1. This is a two-arm metabolic and survival mechanism. MRTX1133 plus USP20 inhibition and PD-1 blockade regressed tumors in preclinical models, but human tissue profiling is not evidence of clinical combination efficacy.

evidence.reference_title: USP20 promotes CD8(+) T cell exhaustion and impairs KRAS(G12D) inhibitor efficacy by orchestrating cholesterol metabolism and autophagy in pancreatic cancer.
evidence.snippet: Mechanistically, KRASG12D transcriptionally upregulated USP20 via EGR1, which simultaneously deubiquitinated and stabilised 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA reductase and ULK1, thereby orchestrating cholesterol metabolism and autophagy-associated survival.

evidence.reference_title: USP20 promotes CD8(+) T cell exhaustion and impairs KRAS(G12D) inhibitor efficacy by orchestrating cholesterol metabolism and autophagy in pancreatic cancer.
evidence.snippet: In preclinical PDAC models, triple therapy with GSK2643943A, MRTX1133 and anti-PD-1 elicited a robust therapeutic response and induced significant tumour regression.

nodes.description: Unintentional weight loss may reflect reduced intake, systemic cancer effects and pancreatic exocrine insufficiency; it can precede diagnosis.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnostic evaluation and staging of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
evidence.snippet: Common signs and symptoms of PDA include abdominal or back pain, jaundice, weight loss, pruritus, and nausea/vomiting.
